articles.title: Jio Platforms' IPO-linked inflows boost rupee; elevated oil prices spur caution
articles.excerpt:
The Indian rupee experienced a notable increase as Jio Platforms' IPO attracted significant foreign investments. Despite this strength, rising oil prices raised concerns among traders about the rupee's sustainability. The rupee closed at 94.46 against the dollar, with earlier gains trimmed by higher Brent crude oil prices. Analysts suggest that the upcoming RBI monetary policy might influence future exchange rates.

articles.title: IMF advises India to let rupee move as first defence amid oil shock
articles.excerpt:
istock photo for BL | Photo Credit: Dmitriy Razinkov

India should allow the dollar-rupee exchange rate to move as the first line of defence amid the ongoing oil shock, an IMF official said on Wednesday.

“Our advice to countries is to use the exchange rate as the first line of defence amid ongoing shocks,” Krishna Srinivasan, Director of the Asia and Pacific Department at the IMF, said at a media briefing in Mumbai. “We would advise India to let the exchange rate move.”

The Reserve Bank of India has intervened heavily to support the rupee via dollar sales from its reserves, a special window to offer dollars to oil companies and reserve requirements for large hedge requirements.

articles.title: Higher Oil Availability Pressures Middle East Crude Benchmarks
articles.excerpt:
Higher Oil Availability Pressures Middle East Crude Benchmarks

Robust crude oil flows out of the Middle East in recent weeks have started to pressure the key metric of strength for physical supply out of the region.

The premium of Oman crude over Dubai, the measure of Middle East’s market strength, has slumped this week to the lowest level since the end of July, to $4.22 per barrel, according to data by General Index cited by Bloomberg.

articles.title: Qatar Offers Lebanon 2 Gas Plants and 20 Years of LNG Piped Through Syria
articles.excerpt:
Higher Oil Availability Pressures Middle East Crude Benchmarks

Qatar is offering to take over Lebanon's power supply problem at no upfront cost to Beirut. A draft program seen by Reuters has Qatar building two gas-fired power plants within three years and QatarEnergy supplying the gas under a 20-year LNG contract, with private financing in place of Lebanese public money. The document leaves payment obligations and guarantees open for negotiation, and Lebanon's state utility currently delivers only a few hours of electricity a day.
